test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the grammatically correct version of the following sentence.

He was youngest than his brother.

options.text: He was younger than his brother.
He was youngest to his brother.
He was too young than his brother.
He was young to his brother.

solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. He was younger than his brother is the correct version.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence "He was youngest than his brother." is incorrect because it improperly uses "youngest" in a comparative context.

• The correct comparative form when comparing two entities is "younger" not "youngest," which is used for superlative comparisons among three or more entities.

• The preposition "than" is correctly used in comparisons, making "younger than" the appropriate phrase to use.

• The correct sentence structure for comparing the age of two people is "Subject + was + younger than + object."

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *He was younger than his brother.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "He was youngest to his brother." - This option is incorrect because "youngest" is a superlative form and "to" is not the correct preposition for comparison in this context.

• "He was too young than his brother." - This option is grammatically incorrect because "too" is not used in standard comparative structures, and "than" is misused here.

• "He was young to his brother." - This option lacks a comparative form and incorrectly uses the preposition "to" for comparison.
